statements.t: (NYSE: NRGV) (“Energy Vault” or “the Company”), a global energy infrastructure company supporting grid reliability and next-generation AI and high-performance computing infrastructure, today announced financial results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 and guidance updates.

“In AI infrastructure, we secured non-recourse financing for 275 MW of Rolls-Royce MTU reciprocating engine generation capacity, advanced our Digital Vault Sulcis development in Italy following its designation as a project of pre-eminent national strategic interest, and started construction of the Snyder AI modular data center project.
During the fourth quarter, we began deliveries to the recently announced 1.25GW hybrid generation and energy storage project supporting AI compute infrastructure in Texas.
We remain focused on efficient project execution for our customers, capital discipline and progressing our development pipeline towards operating assets and long term, recurring EBITDA.”

A reconciliation of projected non-GAAP measures has not been provided because certain information necessary to calculate such measures on a GAAP basis is not available without unreasonable effort or is dependent on the timing of future events outside of our control.

Contingent option bookings are from projects where the Company holds an enforceable exclusive purchase right and intends to exercise that right, even if the option has not been exercised as of period end.

Bookings include agreements and purchase orders for third-party projects and services, IP licensing, and leasing, tolling, energy supply and offtake arrangements associated with energy infrastructure owned or operated by the Company or its affiliates.

For variable payments dependent on energy market conditions, the Company uses forecasts prepared by an independent third-party firm using simulation software that considers current and projected energy market dynamics, historical and forecasted volatility, and location-specific data.

For variable payments dependent on customer consumption or utilization, the Company uses applicable contractual pricing and management’s estimates of expected consumption or utilization, considering customer-provided forecasts, anticipated operating ramp-up, available operating data and other relevant information, as applicable.

Backlog represents estimated future revenue or other income not yet recognized from (i) third-party projects and services, (ii) IP licensing agreements, and (iii) leasing, tolling, energy supply and offtake arrangements associated with energy infrastructure owned or operated by the Company or its affiliates, in each case associated with contracted bookings or contingent option bookings, as defined above.

Contingent option backlog reflects amounts associated with projects where the Company holds an enforceable exclusive purchase right and intends to exercise that right, even if the option has not been exercised as of period end, and is contingent on the Company exercising the applicable purchase right and subsequent project execution.
Our presentation of adjusted EBITDA should not be construed as an inference that our future results will be unaffected by these types of adjustments.

Because of these limitations, adjusted EBITDA should not be considered as a measure of discretionary cash available to us to invest in the growth of our business or as a measure of cash that will be available to use to meet our obligations.
